also: I’d better keep my mouth shut
why don’t you just shut up?

terms.gloss: why don’t you keep quiet? (be quiet!)
terms.grammar: quīn with the indicative: an impatient “why not …?”, really a command
evidence: Plaut. Merc. 2.4.26: Quīn tacēs? — Mūtō imperās. (Lewis & Short s.v. mūtus)
Traupman 106: why don’t you keep quiet?, quīn tū tacēs?
Traupman 104: shut your mouth, obserā ōs tuum!
Traupman 107: shut up!, obserā ōs tuum!
terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase, “bolt your mouth”. Lewis & Short has the figure with palātum, “to be silent” (Catull. 55.21), not with ōs; the everyday command is Tacē!.

terms.grammar: silentium in the accusative; imperative silentium tenē (tenēte)
evidence: Liv. 5.9.4: tribūnī plēbis, cum invītī silentium tenuissent (Lewis & Short s.v. silentium)

phrases.latin: Tacē, occultēmus lūmen et vōcem. — Licet.
phrases.english: Hush, let’s hide the light and our voices. — All right; for a game in the dark.
I’d better keep my mouth shut.
Why don’t you just shut up?
